root_idea.summary: The root centers on the idea of something extending or spreading smoothly, as with straight, non-crisp hair.
root_idea.development: This idea extends to bodily extension and lying outstretched, generosity that is freely extended, abundance, branching lineages, and things spread between or over spaces. These developments are broader semantic orientations and are not all direct meanings of the Qur'anic form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Qur'anic plural is presented under the normalized singular dictionary citation form سِبْطٌ.

senses.definition: A tribal lineage or branch of descendants traced to a common forefather; in the Qur'an, the Israelite tribal branches or communities associated with Jacob.
senses.usage_conditions: The attested Qur'anic form is the plural أَسْبَاط. It is used collectively for tribal lineages and communities, including the twelve communities mentioned in 7:160; the contextual translations “descendants” and “tribes” reflect this lineage-based collective sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become lank, straight, and not crisp; lank or non-crisp, especially of hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal and adjectival usages describe hair that lies straight rather than curly or compact.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tall, long-boned, extended-limbed, or well-proportioned in build.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or to the length and evenness of the limbs and bodily frame.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be easy and liberal in beneficence; to be generous, bountiful, or munificent, including bestowing gifts successively and abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person’s beneficence, including the construction سَبَطَ عَلَيْهِ العَطَاءَ, “he bestowed successive large gifts upon him.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abundant, extensive, and successive, said of rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive usage for rain that pours broadly and continuously.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be affected with fever.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive verb describes a person overcome by fever, including fever associated with trembling or weakness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cast a young one or fetus abortively, before its form is complete.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said especially of a camel or ewe that miscarries, including after the young one's hair has grown but before full development.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall or lie extended upon the ground and become unable to move.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The state may result from beating, disease, weakness, medicine, or another cause; the expression أَسْبَطَ بِالأَرْضِ also means to cling or remain down upon the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become silent and still, sometimes with the eyes lowered toward the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A state of silence or stillness attributed to fear or fright.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To close the eyes or eyelids in sleep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction أَسْبَطَ فِي نَوْمِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feign negligence, inattention, or heedlessness toward a matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَنِ الأَمْرِ for pretending to disregard an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grandchild, whether the child of a son or of a daughter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is أَسْبَاط. The broader Classical usage includes both lines of descent, despite a later popular distinction that restricts the word to daughters’ children.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A generation that comes after another generation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective generational usage distinct from the specific kinship sense “grandchild.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A palm tree whose fruit ripens at the end of summer or the hot season.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical regional usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tall desert grass or sand plant, especially the fresh form of a plant otherwise called حَلِيّ or نَصِيّ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is described as good pasture, eaten by camels and other livestock, and having a tall, grain-bearing growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tree with many branches arising from a single stem or root.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical usage connected in the lexical discussion with the notion of branching.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Metonymically, a foreigner or non-Arab.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application associated with lank hair and contrasted with the term جَعْدٌ as applied to an Arab.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fever, including fever accompanied by shivering or trembling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is associated with the bodily extension or relaxation caused by the illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A month between winter and spring, corresponding to February in the older Syrian calendar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A calendrical term of Greek or Syrian usage; it precedes آذَارُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sweepings or collected household refuse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to material swept from house courts, ordinarily discarded each day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where sweepings and dirt are thrown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same noun may denote either the refuse itself or the dumping place, depending on context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hair that falls out during combing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete usage for combed-out hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A palm raceme with its fruit stalks and fresh ripe dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional botanical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A roofed passage or covered structure between two walls or houses, with a road or thoroughfare beneath it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The structure forms a covered way connecting or spanning the sides of a passage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hanging the head in grief or anxiety and appearing lax or slack in body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in descriptions of a person’s dejected, drooping posture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a state of sickness or debility in which one neither moves nor speaks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a sick person left motionless and silent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land abounding in the plant سَبَطٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine adjectival description of land rich in the named desert grass or plant.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Falling or lying extended and unable to move.
Grandchild through either son or daughter.
Israelite tribal branches and the Qur'anic twelve-community construction.
A palm tree with late-ripening fruit.
Desert grass and the separately stated many-branched tree usage.
Liberal or munificent hands and beneficence.
Calendrical month between winter and spring.
Drooping grief posture and the distinct sick, motionless state.

cautions: The Qur'anic occurrences are all in the plural form أَسْبَاط; the singular سِبْطٌ also has broader Classical meanings, including “grandchild,” that should not be conflated with the Qur'anic tribal sense.
